thread:
alex: Heads-up — us-west dedicated pool seeing a throughput drop starting ~14:12PT. Multiple worker restarts and a couple GPU OOMs. Repro rate ~25% for the affected nodes.

maria: Noted. Any recent rollouts or kernel changes?

alex: No user-facing deploys. We did push a kernel-selection heuristic tweak yesterday to prefer the low-latency kernels for small batches.

raj: Alloc logs show a bunch of page-sweeper delays around the same time. Could be GC/backpressure interacting with allocator.

alloc-bot: [alert] worker-42 restarted due to CUDA OOM (pid=2311) at 2025-10-07T14:14:05Z.

alex: Pasting the minimal timeline we grabbed from prom and node logs:
```
14:11:40 - small batch surge from noisy-tenant T-152
14:12:03 - first worker restart (OOM) on node gpu-12
14:12:07 - page-sweeper job queued, delayed ~120s
14:12:30 - kernel fallback triggered for >512 seq (switched to generic kernel)
14:13:00 - kv-cache eviction spike: 85% of entries evicted in 30s
14:14:05 - second OOM, alloc throttling engages
```

maria: Interesting — fallback to generic kernel would increase memory working set per request. Combined with kv-evicts that amplifies OOMs.

tessa: Can we see the kernel selection debug output from the runtime on gpu-12?

alex: Pasted from runtime debug:
```
[14:11:59] candidate_kernels=[fast_small, fast_med, generic]
[14:12:00] score(fast_small)=0.47, score(fast_med)=0.62, score(generic)=0.80
[14:12:00] selected=fast_med (but failing tail-latency).
[14:12:30] fallback_rule: if kv_cache_miss_rate>0.3 && seq>256 => select=generic
[14:12:30] fallback selected=generic
```

raj: That fallback rule is new — might be too aggressive. generic kernel uses a different allocator path that pins bigger chunks and defeats page-sweeper heuristics.

jamal: I see repeated pci stalls in the nvidia driver logs around 14:12:20. Could be DMA pressure from large transfers during generic kernel paths.

alex: Also saw this in the profiler (aggregated across affected nodes):
```
metric: gpu_mem_alloc_rate => spike +2.1x
metric: pci_stall_time_ms => 14:12..14:16 average 23ms (baseline 3ms)
metric: kv_cache_miss_rate => peaked 0.42
metric: effective_batch_size => dropped 60% due to throttling
```

maria: So chain: noisy tenant causes small-batch surge -> heuristic flips kernel -> generic kernel increases allocation pattern -> page-sweeper delayed -> kv evictions and PCIe stalls -> OOMs and restarts.

tessa: Are the page-sweeper config values on these nodes non-default? Sweep interval or sweep budget?

alex: They were default, but node gpu-12's sweeper thread got starved (scheduling trace attached). OS showed high softirq and io wait during the window.

raj: Two mitigation ideas: 1) revert fallback rule so we don't switch to generic on miss spikes, 2) bump sweeper frequency/budget temporarily for the pool, and 3) isolate noisy tenant T-152 to a capped queue.

jamal: I can patch an emergency knob to disable the fallback rule for the us-west dedicated pool. Push can be done via config roll to master with runtime hot-reload.

alloc-bot: [action] creating ticket INF-6672 for urgent config roll.

alex: Going to run a targeted restart on the 3 impacted workers after disabling fallback. Will also add a temporary tenant tag to throttle T-152.

maria: Also add a short-term increase to the page-sweeper budget on those nodes: set sweep_interval=30s -> 5s and sweep_pages_budget=512 -> 2048. Keep track of CPU impact.

tessa: We should also capture a flame graph of allocator hot paths pre/post change to validate we regain expected memory churn.

alex: Rolling config now — disabling fallback on us-west dedicated (rolling over 6 nodes) and bumping sweeper budget on nodes gpu-10..gpu-15.

alloc-bot: [info] config-roll started for pool=us-west-dedicated, change_id=cfg-20251007-01.

14:25 - after changes: one remaining node reported higher tail-latency but no new OOMs. Throughput recovering to ~95% of baseline.

jamal: Good. We should prepare a permanent fix: either make the kernel-selection cost model account for sweeper delay/pci stalls, or change generic kernel to use smaller pinned-chunk strategy.

raj: Agreed. Also add unit test for synthetic noisy-tenant patterns to ensure fallback isn't triggered under high miss-rate bursts.

maria: Follow-ups:
- jamal: prototype smaller-chunk allocator for generic kernel (ETA 3d)
- tessa: add allocator flame graphs and dashboards for sweep delay (ETA 1d)
- alex: write post-incident runbook entry and add noisy-tenant auto-isolation rule (ETA 2d)

alex: quick note — no customer data exposure; incident confined to dedicated pool.

tessa: Marking incident as "mitigated" for now. Will re-open if OOMs recur. :white_check_mark:

alex: Thanks all. Saving logs and attaching perf traces to INF-6672.

alloc-bot: [resolved] worker restarts subsided. Monitoring for 2h window.
